kind: live read-only snapshots taken while riding and after a crash, evaluated offline; NOT an observed in-game invocation of the refresh

route.player: registered snow actor -> +0x168 runtime -> +0x6e8 main / +0xb90 rider body -> +0x30 metadata -> +0x20 owner -> +0x20 controller (capture.py route, unchanged)
route.extra_roots: up to six bodies with nonempty +0x80 rings or provider-tree endpoints, enumerated from the controller found by the closed-loop world scan; each analysed with the same harness as main/rider

method: native director startup (explore.py, director plugin, hands-off title/offline notice/map); bounded SendInput holds of scan 17 (forward) on the verified game window; a private coordinator polled the player chain read-only at about 4 Hz and, when a player body had a controller and a +0x80 head (auto) or on operator request, held the world Step job through the snow host, read every region twice and resumed. Offline, analyze.py ran the Python chain on a copy and native 18b8860 in Unicorn over the snapshot (recording stubs for stack probe, allocator, pool-return blocks and group processing; every uncaptured read is a gap), comparing selections, service-call sequences and all bytes.
verdict: PASS: 63/63 native-vs-Python comparisons over 11 live snapshots; 55 exercised selection/rebuild/retire on nonempty +0x80 rings (max 20 rows), 8 took the empty-ring early return; 0 mismatched bytes, 0 coverage gaps, no Python or native errors.
limits: Snapshots are evaluated offline; no in-game invocation of 18b8860 by controller event 0 was observed.
Reads are sequential while the Step job is held; jobs outside Step may run. Unchanged second-pass reads do not make a snapshot atomic.
Service routines 18e2de0 (group processing), pool-return blocks and the allocator are recording stubs: their argument sequences are compared, not their effects.
Most roots carried one or two +0x80 links; the largest live inputs were 10- and 20-row selections. Retire divisors and allocation growth beyond one reallocation were not exercised.

A combined forward+jump hold (scans 17 and 57) was rejected by the input helper; the crash/ragdoll snapshots came from riding into terrain, not a deliberate jump. No landing-contact moment was isolated. Snapshot names air/post1-3 are operator labels set at trigger time; the screenshot shows the rider tumbling in a crash, with both player bodies detached (null controller) and the ragdoll/world bodies carrying the rings.
In ride-01 the host socket closed after the crash (KO screen), ending capture early; ride-02 had one host resume reply step_not_resumed while the step counter continued to advance.
Heap addresses, raw bytes and snapshots are private and not published.
